raw_response:
I'm 72 this year, and I've been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. Never went to school — can't read a word — but I know every corner of my fields. My wife and I are the only ones left at home. Our son works in Shijiazhuang, sends a little money now and then, but the farm is what feeds us. At my age, I can't take big risks. I do what I know.

I keep 12 mu for wheat and then maize after, and 8 mu for cotton. That's the split I've had for years. The wheat went in last October, same week as always. I bought the seed from the supply shop in town — not the fancy kind, but the one that grows steady. For the base fertilizer, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, same as my brother-in-law does on his place. Now it's spring, and the wheat is waking up. When it starts jointing, I'll topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Last year I tried a little less on one plot and the wheat turned yellow — never again. I'll water it three times: once now to green it up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. The pump takes electricity and that costs me, but dry wheat is no wheat.

After we cut the wheat in early June, those 12 mu need to turn around fast for maize. Sometimes we only have five or six days. I'll hire Old Wang's tractor to plow, then plant the maize seed right away. One bag of compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, and if July is dry like last year, I'll spread some urea and give it a good watering. Maybe two waterings total — maize doesn't beg like wheat does. I'll need a couple of young hands to help plant, because my back won't let me bend that quick anymore.

The cotton is on the other 8 mu. I plant it in mid-April. It needs less fertilizer than wheat — about four-fifths of a bag of compound at planting, then some urea when it flowers. Cotton is where the money goes on spraying. Those bollworms never sleep. I'll spray three times, maybe four if I see them early. Picking is the hard part. My wife and I can do some, but we hire the women from the village for the main picking. My knees can't handle bending all day now.

I'm not changing anything this year. The fertilizer price went up at the shop, so I'm certainly not using more. I'll do exactly what I did last year. If the weather is normal, the wheat should give me about 420 kg per mu, the maize about 480, and the cotton maybe 230 kg of lint. I need enough to live, pay for my medicine, and keep a little cash in my pocket for when the pump breaks.
